note: Public decisions listing of the hosted provider as of 2026-11-14 (https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models?output_modalities=decisions) and its model guide as of 2026-11-14: context length 262144 tokens for state plus questions, an input price in the listing's pricing.prompt (cost_in, cents per million tokens; the int column rounds it down to 4) and a free output. Check before relying on it. The newest release of the model family (GH #1525); the guide documents no breaking change against 1.13, only the Box question 1.13 refused, and a long-context mode above about 32000 bytes of text that the provider calls slower and less accurate. A typed decisions model, not a chat model: wire_dialect 'decisions' marks the protocol, and only a cell born with provider 'decisions' is resolved to this row. One live call on 2026-11-14 (choice, noul and score in the cell's wire form) answered 200 in 216 ms. The row names no endpoint: a push leaves the decider on the base_url its set gives it (PRESENTER_DECIDE_BASE_URL), so it never moves the decider to an origin outside its base_url_allow. max_output 0: a decisions row answers typed decisions, not completions, so no output limit applies (GH #1037). input_hard 262144 = the whole window (a decisions call has no completion to leave room for), input_soft 65536 = 25 % of it; no cache price is listed, so cost_cached_in and cost_cache_write are 0 (R-HK-15/16). Window rates (GH #1085): chars_per_token 3: the cell's cautious default, stated. Not measured. The package's decision_calibration (GH #1558) is an isotonic fit of the model's raw probabilities on a synthetic question bank, as of 2026-11-16.
strengths: Typed decisions only: answers choice, yes/no and scale questions about one state, with probabilities, for a fraction of a cent. Generates no text and calls no tools.

note: A local row: the model as an OpenAI-compatible vLLM server serves it on the operator's own hardware, read on 2026-10-07 from the server's own GET /v1/models. context_window 150000 = the max_model_len that answer reports. The row names no endpoint: the address of a local server is private to its host, so a push leaves the cell on the base_url its set gives it. Local inference bills nothing, so every price is 0 and there is no input_cache_read price to read. Cache: vLLM caches prefixes automatically (prefix caching) and names no expiry, so the TTL is 0 and the llm cell stamps none. Parameters measured with workshop/tools/llm-conformance on 2026-10-05: a local server answers every sampling field with 200, so none is verified and the row carries no supported_params -- the cell sends them unverified, as before. max_output 50000 = the room input_hard leaves in the window: the server lists no completion limit of its own, prompt and answer share max_model_len. input_hard 100000 = the context window less 50k tokens of room for an answer (a longer one is continued), rounded down to 10k; input_soft 25000 = 25 % of input_hard, the size from which a rebuild of the window pays (R-HK-15/16). Status explicit: reached only by name -- a start value, a replacement, a tier -- never by prose or a ranked select, where a price of 0 would win every search. Window rates (GH #1085): chars_per_token 3: the cell's cautious default, stated; a local server refuses a prompt past its window, so the estimate stays high. Not measured.
strengths: A model served on the operator's own hardware behind an OpenAI-compatible server: no per-token price and no data leaving the machine, with a window far smaller than the hosted rows. Reached by name only.

note: Public listing of the hosted provider as of 2026-10-07 (its embeddings model list): context length 8192 tokens, an input price per token (cost_in, converted to cents per million tokens), no completion price. The embed cells of the memory hive and the file space call it (MEMORY_EMBED_MODEL, their default), and the file space reads its window as `embed_input_soft_fallback` (GH #1085). input_hard 8192 = the whole input limit (an embedding call has no answer to leave room for); input_soft 2048 = 25 % of it, so a section sized at three characters a token stays inside the limit even where one character is one token. max_output 0: an embedding answers vectors, not completions. Window rates (GH #1085): chars_per_token 4: the provider's public tokenizer guidance of about four characters of English a token. Not measured.
strengths: Embeddings only: one vector per input text, for the semantic search over memories and files. Generates no text and calls no tools.

note: Public model overview and price list of the provider as of 2026-10-17 (its own documentation, models overview and pricing): id, context window 1000000 and list price in cents per million tokens; max_output 128000 = the max output of the synchronous Messages API. The list tiers the price by prompt length: cost_in / cost_out are the base step up to 100k prompt tokens, price_tiers the step above (GH #1318). Check before relying on it. A native row (GH #1243): wire_dialect 'messages' names the provider's native Messages wire. GH #1273: chat and messages rows are one pool, so a push moves an llm cell onto this row and back -- the push names provider 'anthropic', this base_url (the cell appends /messages; it must be in the cell's base_url_allow) and cred_ref cred:anthropic, the vault name the cell asks the access hive for. The key is never in the row: the vault holds it, and the access catalogue (a cred_refs row of class llm) says the cell's grant may fetch it. Status explicit: reached only by name -- a start value, a replacement, a tier -- never by prose or a ranked select; no shipped tier points here. Cache: explicit cache_control breakpoints with a five-minute default lifetime and a minimum prefix of 512 tokens, per the provider's public prompt-caching documentation as of 2026-10-16; 300 s is that default, a hit renews it. cost_cached_in / cost_cache_write: the list's cache read price (the input_cache_read of the other rows) and its five-minute cache write price, base tier. input_hard 950000 = the context window less 50k tokens of room for an answer, rounded down to 10k; input_soft 200000 = the owner's hard stop for the window (UX before price, R-38-2, 2026-11-05); the price step stays in price_tiers and enters the curator's cost rule (GH #1431). Length continuations stay off: a continuation hands the cut text back as the assistant's turn (a prefill), which the provider refuses on this model generation, so a cell on this row keeps length_continuations at 0; not measured. Window rates (GH #1085): chars_per_token 3: the cell's cautious three, as the provider's current tokenizer counts more tokens for the same text than its older one; tokens_per_image 1600: the provider's vision documentation (about width x height / 750, at most about 1600 for an image it does not downscale). strengths: The small Claude model on its provider's native Messages API, with tools, vision and adaptive reasoning, for high-volume work such as conversation, classification, extraction and routing; the cheapest Claude row here. Reached by name only.

Check before relying on it. An open-weight model served by several hosts behind the gateway. Provider (GH #1260, Lab P1): the package pins the host crusoe/bf16 through provider_extra (provider.order with allow_fallbacks false), measured against four other fast hosts of the endpoints listing on 2026-10-19 -- nebius/fp4 p50 325 ms with one tool argument that was not valid JSON, cerebras/fp16 333 ms with a p95 of 1617 ms, groq 337 ms, coreweave/fp4 667 ms; the gateway's default routing measured 1624 ms the same day. A fallback is forbidden: it would serve a slow host under this time. The prices are the pinned host's in the endpoints listing of 2026-10-19. Cache: the listing names a cache read price but no lifetime (as of 2026-10-19), so the TTL is 0 and the llm cell stamps none; cost_cached_in: the pinned host's pricing.input_cache_read (no discount on its prompt price), no cache write price. input_hard 80000 = the context window less 50k tokens of room for an answer, rounded down to 10k; input_soft 20000 = 25 % of input_hard (R-HK-15/16). Parameters measured with workshop/tools/llm-conformance on 2026-10-19: temperature, top_p, reasoning and reasoning_effort taken. Status explicit (GH #1025): reached only by a replacement, a tier or a start value, never by a prose translation or a ranked select. Window rates (GH #1085): chars_per_token 4: the provider's public tokenizer guidance of about four characters of English a token. Text only. Not measured. response_ms 231 (GH #1260): the p50 of 20 tool calls at a window of about 4k tokens with four tools and no stream, measured with workshop/tools/llm-conformance --latency 20 --provider-order crusoe/bf16 on 2026-10-19 with reasoning at effort low, which this endpoint requires (switching reasoning off is refused); the package sends the reasoning object {"effort": "medium"} (owner ruling OR-EF-18, GH #1300); until GH #1300 it sent {"effort": "low"}, the effort of the latency measurement. It sends the object, not the reasoning_effort shorthand, because a push resets every other key to its birth value and a cell born with reasoning switched off would keep the switch, which outranks the shorthand (review C-1); a p95 of 333 ms; 20 of 20 calls hit the expected tool. Forced tool call (GH #1260, OR-WG-9, wave lab BL2): the pinned host is dropped by the gateway's tool compatibility filter when tool_choice is required (HTTP 404, the turn went silent), so the package says tool_choice_required false and the cell sends auto -- 20 of 20 right tool calls there, p50 555 ms.
strengths: An open-weight reasoning model with tools and structured output, text only, for agentic steps at a low price.
